problem: The sentence 'Aluminium alloys are weaker; the same 159 MPa would be close to failure' is wrong as a general statement. Many wrought structural aluminium alloys (for example the 2xxx, 6xxx and 7xxx families) have yield strengths of 200 MPa or more, comparable to or above mild steel, so 159 MPa is not near failure in them. Only some cast and pure grades are that weak. A student can carry away the false rule 'aluminium fails around 160 MPa'.
fix: Replace with: 'Aluminium is not automatically weaker: many wrought alloys have yield strengths of 200 MPa or more, while some cast grades are far weaker. Never assume a strength; take the value for the actual alloy from a table.'

where: Section 2, the paragraph beginning 'V/A_s gives an average'
problem: 'Zero at its edges and peaks in the middle' is loose for a solid circular section. The shear stress is zero at the top and bottom points of the section (the ends of the diameter perpendicular to the load), not at every edge; the peak is at the centre and is 4/3 of the average, not just 'higher'.
fix: Say: 'The real shear stress on a solid circular rivet section is zero at the top and bottom of the section and reaches 4V/3A at the centre — one-third above the average. Simple design uses the average V/A_s.'

problem: '159.2 kN/anything is wrong on the unit alone' reads awkwardly and the logic is inverted: a force divided by an area is a stress, so the error is writing a force where a stress is asked, not the division itself.
fix: Write: 'Stress is force per area; an answer in kN is a force, not a stress, and scores zero however right the number looks.'
